architecture: Extraction, source encoding, UTF-16/source maps, permissions, owner snapshots, conflict checks, checkpoints and constructor operations belong to ESKA.
Explorer renders models and status, transports LSP requests and applies checked native edits with Undo/Redo.
The provider-level protected view shares the common backend snapshot; ordinary file tabs remain editable under the accepted conflict-checking contract.
The existing published analyzer process receives an in-memory BSL projection; no fork, embedded kernel, per-edit subprocess or additional source file is used.

limitations: Windows, macOS, Microsoft VS Code, Remote and other IDE adapters are unverified.
XML query context analysis and parameter completion remain unavailable in the checked published-server contract. Full hover/definition/reference coverage inside SDBL is not separately accepted.
The first constructor subset accepts typed expressions; no metadata picker or join dependency reordering. Unsupported constructs remain exact source text.
Unaccepted visual operations are memory-only. A backend crash preserves the previously acknowledged canonical draft and requires explicit resume.
Comment dialog choices are scripted in acceptance; production webview buttons are exercised through actual Chromium DOM in normal installed ru/en windows.
Performance cohorts use a synthetic query in an added writable module in the isolated full buhmfo application with five extensions. An existing vendor-prohibited module is checked separately.
Cold means fresh private profile and ESKA cache removal; OS page cache is not flushed. CPU/IO figures include verbose native-window logging.
VSCodium may retain closed native text models temporarily. ESKA owns no remaining query sessions, language views/tasks/timers/states or private draft data after the series.
The canonical repository guide is updated; the separate website checkout on main was not edited.
